steps.text: Iron rusts, but only under certain conditions. Let's find out exactly what iron needs to rust.
Watch the three test tubes: one with both air and water, one with water but no air, and one with dry air but no water.
Only the tube with BOTH air and water shows rust. Water alone or air alone isn't enough.
So iron rusts only when air (oxygen) AND water are both present. That's why oiling or painting iron — which keeps out air and water — prevents rusting.

coach.mission: Find out which condition makes iron rust.
whenStuck: Compare the three tubes and see which one rusts.
Look for the tube that has both air and water.
whenWrong: Air alone doesn't rust iron, and water alone doesn't either — it needs both.
Only the tube with both air and water shows rust.
whenCorrect: Right — iron needs both air and water to rust.
Exactly — remove either air or water and the iron stays shiny.
coach.done: You've discovered iron rusts only with both air and water. Explore more, or move on when you're ready.
